predecessors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Aleppo, taken from the Fatimid governor in 1025

successors.name: Uqaylid dynasty
successors.text: Aleppo, taken by Muslim ibn Quraysh in June 1080

ledger.x: 1014: Salih ibn Mirdas escapes prison and founds the Mirdasid emirate.
1015: Manbij and Balis.
1022: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa.
1025: the central Syrian domains.
1025: Salih takes Aleppo.
1029: the Fatimids move against Salih's Syria; he is killed at al-Uqhuwana on the shore of Lake Tiberias (12 or 25 May 1029).
1029: the Fatimids take the central Syrian domains.
1029: the fight ends with the Fatimid conquest of the central Syrian domains; Nasr holds Aleppo.

1038: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa are in Numayrid hands by 1039/40; the Mirdasid page says only that the Mirdasids "had also since lost control of Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to the Numayrids" and the Nasr ibn Salih page has no dates on it (the Shabib ibn Waththab article does not exist at that title).
1038: the Fatimid governor of Damascus takes Aleppo.
1040: Thimal gains Raqqa and al-Rafiqa.
1042: Thimal recovers Aleppo.
1056: Mani' ibn Shabib of the Numayrids moves against Thimal over Raqqa.
1057: the fighting over Raqqa ends with Mani' holding it (October 1057).
1057: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa pass to the Numayrids.
1058: Thimal steps down and Aleppo passes to the Fatimid governor.
1059: Mani' of the Numayrids takes al-Rahba.
1060: Mahmud ibn Nasr, the Mirdasid nephew, seizes Aleppo in September; Thimal regained it on 23 April 1061 and Atiyya gave it up to Mahmud in 1065 (internal Mirdasid succession).
1061: Atiyya retakes al-Rahba for Thimal.
1062: Atiyya ibn Salih takes Raqqa.
1080: Muslim ibn Quraysh takes Aleppo.
1080: the Mirdasid dynasty ends with the loss of Aleppo.

wars.name: Battle of al-Uqhuwana (Mirdasid-Fatimid war)
wars.outcome: Salih allied with the Banu Tayy and Banu Kalb in 1023 and was killed at al-Uqhuwana on the eastern shore of Lake Tiberias in May 1029; the Fatimids took his central Syrian domains.

wars.name: Battle of Azaz
wars.outcome: Nasr "routed his forces at the Battle of Azaz (1030)" after Romanos III led the assault in person in the summer; no border moved.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Aleppo (1038)
wars.outcome: Anushtakin al-Dizbari killed Nasr in battle and seized Aleppo in summer 1038; Thimal fled to the Jazira.

wars.name: Thimal's Fatimid campaigns (1048-1050)
wars.outcome: A Fatimid army under Ibn Hamdan withdrew after flooding at Shildi in autumn 1048 (it had taken Hama earlier that year); Thimal destroyed Rifq's army at Jabal Jawshin in August 1050 and peace followed late in 1050.

wars.name: Mirdasid-Numayrid war over Raqqa (1056-1057)
wars.outcome: Hostilities began in April 1056 when Thimal refused Mani's demand to leave Raqqa; Mani', backed by the Fatimid envoy al-Mu'ayyad and al-Basasiri, received Raqqa and al-Rafiqa in October 1057 (captured, or handed over under pressure per Ibn Shaddad); Atiyya…

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Aleppo (1080)
wars.outcome: Muslim ibn Quraysh took Aleppo in June 1080 after its inhabitants offered to hand it over; the Mirdasid dynasty ended.

certainty.note: Tribal emirate of fortress towns and caravan cities; the pages give towns and no frontiers.
